record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; the paper and code were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports applying refusal steering in MoE models, a new architecture setting, and gives results. It describes an extension of Arditi et al.'s approach, not an explicit reproduction.
record.gate_note: The README reports an aggregate ActAdd attack-success result and expert-level recovery results. The listed scripts and experiment outputs are not evidence that other listed experiments ran; no unreported script results are included.
record.test_reason: The README reports that the Arditi difference-in-means refusal direction, applied with ActAdd, suppresses refusal in three MoE instruct models (>65% ASR). This is V1's causal claim tested in a new architecture. Only a summary is available; the paper itself was not read.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. Refusal steering transfers to the MoE models. Single experts carry substantial but incomplete signal, and part of the signal lies outside the FFN sublayer. Routing-frequency differences do not predict effective steering directions.
record.recipe_differences: The README says the repo builds on the Arditi refusal-steering code and includes an Arditi direction-generation pipeline, then extends activation-addition steering to MoE models. The reported finding concerns steering; it does not report the original claim's all-layer, all-position ablation.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports results across system-prompt settings and says expert recovery differs between independently searched and ActAdd-matched intervention sites.

fits_no_version.finding: Single-expert steering recovers up to 78% of ActAdd's effect at a freely searched site, but 54% at the ActAdd site.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In MoE models, refusal-relevant steering signal is partly carried by individual experts and partly lies outside the FFN sublayer.

fits_no_version.finding: Experts selected by harmful-vs-harmless routing-frequency differences do not reliably yield effective steering directions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Routing-frequency 'safety experts' do not identify where the refusal direction's steering signal lives.

record.problems: Evidence here is limited to README summaries: no per-model or per-system-prompt ASR values, baseline, uncertainty, or general-capability result is provided. Expert-recovery findings lack model-specific results. Code was not read or run.
record.rows_left_out: No additional experimental results are reported in the README. The file list shows scripts and datasets but does not establish that those experiments ran.

untested.parts: Directional ablation at all layers and positions; adding the direction to harmless prompts to induce refusal; general capability preservation; per-model refusal rates against a baseline.
The README mentions possible nonlinear or entangled structure and a two-pathway account only as open questions, not as results.

missing.what: Per-model and per-system-prompt ASR, the unsteered baseline refusal rate, and any capability or benchmark results; these are presumably in the paper.
The routing-based safety-expert result has no row.

record.verdict_notes: Evidence is README-only. The arXiv ID and dates look anomalous (2606, pushed 2026) but are recorded as given. The V1 verdict rests on one aggregate floor statistic and should be revisited once the paper is read.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not report projecting the direction out at every layer and position, adding it to harmless requests, or measuring general capability. It reports ActAdd steering and attack success, not a direct ablation.
No released-model weight edit or abliteration result is reported.
No result tests whether attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
The expert-level results do not test whether refusal is better described by an affine structure, a cone, or a dominant direction plus others.
No separate measure of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
The README reports steering in MoE models, but does not test whether the same direction transfers across languages, model variants, or from base to instruct models.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing is reported.

rows.measure: Attack success rate under refusal steering
rows.note: One aggregate statement across the three models and system-prompt settings; individual results are not given. The README characterizes steering as suppressing refusal, but does not report an unsteered baseline or complete refusal removal.
rows.check: Aggregate floor only (>65% ASR across models and system prompts), with no unsteered baseline and no per-model values. The README's 'transfers cleanly' wording suggests a strong effect, but a floor of 65% may be well short of the near-complete removal the original reports. The operation is ActAdd, presumably subtracting the direction; sign and coefficient are not stated. Partial is kept as the conservative reading.
